    Predecessors #

    auslander' is Auslander's argument started from a given nonzero map: if the objects of a class P (indecomposable, nonzero, of bounded dimension) have right almost split families inside P, any indecomposable N with a nonzero map into a P-object is isomorphic to a P-object.

    For each nonzero indecomposable we choose the family given by a decomposition of a minimal right almost split map (minRASFam); the predecessors of U (PredC U) are U and, recursively, the sources of these families. If the predecessors of U have bounded dimension, every indecomposable with a nonzero map into U is isomorphic to a predecessor (iso_pred_of_hom).

    ∃ (X : FDMod k A), P X ∧ ∃ (f : N ⟶ X), Function.Bijective ⇑(FDMod.lin f)
